newsitem.title: USA: Plains cattle trade slow after hefty sales-private.
newsitem.headline: Plains cattle trade slow after hefty sales-private.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold in light trade Thursday, with prices quietly slipping to $63.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from large sales this week, feedlot sources said.
Sales volume Thursday was at a trickle compared with the flood of trading that swept the markets this week, pushing Kansas volume to a record high weekly movement of 142,300 head.
Thursday's Kansas sales were pegged at 100 heifers that will likely grade select and choice, USDA reported.
About 400 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, which brought weekly movement there to 131,100, USDA statistics showed.
This week's brisk trading was tied to active sales last Friday of cattle not sold during the week when cattle owners and packers had been locked in a stalemate.

Another round of active sales on Tuesday expanded the weekly figure further and contributed to depletion of most showlists, but at $64.00, down $1.00 from last week, feedlot sources said. Those sales were followed by Thursday's thin trade down another $1 at $63.00.
Fed cattle prices this week crumbled under the weight of large supplies and weak beef prices, sources said.
Declines also were tied to outlooks for large supplies of cattle reaching market weight this summer, feedlot sources said.
